extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural researchers, PIs, program officers, research administrators, and grant applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Informal commentary and practical guidance about NIH review processes, funding policies (IDC/SNAP), fellowship (F31) selection, and study section operations affecting grant submission and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR triage cutoff (discussion eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some non-public information points to CSR continuing to triage grant applications at about the 33% line, instead of the traditional 50% line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational cutoff determining which applications are discussed vs triaged. The post describes downstream effects: more proposals triaged means many two-day meetings could be accomplished in one day, less SRO time preparing discussion resumes, fewer SROs required, and potential cost savings. Use this cutoff as an implicit selection filter for which applications will receive full discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer honorarium policy
rubrics_metrics.description: There would be savings from cutting the usual reviewer honorarium from $400 to $200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer compensation level is a policy lever that may affect reviewer recruitment/retention and budget calculations for study section operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section composition obligation (geographic & institutional diversity)
rubrics_metrics.description: SROs have an obligation to constitute study sections with an eye to geographic and institutional diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assembling reviewers, staff should consider geographic and institutional representation (including inclusion of reviewers from AREA/COBRE/underfunded institutions). This is an explicit staffing requirement that affects reviewer selection and perceived fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carnegie R1 classification thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Research 1: Very High Spending and Doctorate Production, now defined by a clear threshold of $50 million in total research spending and 70 research doctorates awarded annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carnegie classification criteria can serve as institutional eligibility/benchmark metrics when describing institutional research capacity in grant narratives or program analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: F31 eligibility (stage requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: F31 applicants 'must have advanced to the stage of dissertation research at the time of award.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should only apply when they are at dissertation research stage; budget and training expectations (stipend, tuition/fees) align with this stage. Ensure eligibility is documented in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: F31 selection criteria (funding decision factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection process: 'Scientific and technical merit of the proposed project as determined by scientific peer review. Availability of funds. Relevance of the proposed project to program priorities.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the explicit factors the ICs use when making funding decisions after peer review; applicants should focus on project merit and alignment with program priorities, but funding is also constrained by available funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: F31 'Promote Diversity' FOA language and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The diversity FOA 'encourages the recruitment of potential students from the categories spelled out in the NIH Statement of Interest in Diversity' and 'application must include a statement from an institutional official indicating "how the candidate’s participation will further the goals of the fellowship program to promote diversity in health-related research."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FOA lists categories (A) racial and ethnic groups, (B) individuals with disabilities, (C) individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds, and (D) a note on women from these categories. The FOA does not prioritize among these categories. Prepare the institutional statement to explicitly address how the candidate furthers diversity goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of diversity in peer review (no reviewer weighting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The F31 submitted under the parent and the diversity FOA are not reviewed any differently. 'The reviewers are not asked to weigh in on the match to the NIH request to merely recruit underrepresented individuals.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers evaluate scientific/technical merit; they are not asked to evaluate the applicant's contribution to diversity. Programmatic officers/ICs handle programmatic relevance and diversity considerations at funding stage, not during peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNAP principles (Streamlined Noncompeting Award Process)
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of SNAP, NIH staff assures that proposed costs are 'allowable, allocable, reasonable, and necessary' and the budget is negotiated for the entire competitive segment to eliminate annual direct cost negotiations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNAP eligibility and implementation mean fewer annual financial documents are required (programmatic progress report, Federal Cash Transactions Report, Financial Status Report). Applicants/awardees should ensure initial budget negotiation satisfies allowability/allocability/ reasonableness/necessity standards for all years of the competitive segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryforward policy for SNAP-eligible grants
rubrics_metrics.description: SNAP-eligible grants are basically pre-approved for 25% or less carryforward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators on SNAP awards can generally carry forward up to 25% of prior year's budget without additional negotiation; verify with assigned program officer for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Cost (IDC) standardization policy (NOT-OD-25-068)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental Guidance: 'there will be a standard indirect rate of 15% across all NIH grants for indirect costs in lieu of a separately negotiated rate for indirect costs in every grant.' Applied to new grants and retroactively to existing grants for go-forward expenses from Feb 10, 2025 forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy standardizes IDC recovery at 15%, which will shift many costs previously covered by F&A into direct cost charges by institutions. Applicants and institutions must plan budgets and institutional charging practices accordingly; expect institutions to reassign expenses to direct cost categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of purely administrative personnel on R-mech grants
rubrics_metrics.description: It is asserted that 'it is not legal to put purely administrative personnel on a NIH R-mech grant' and that such costs 'may' be allowable on major projects, such as P-mechs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing budgets, expect that purely administrative positions are generally not allowable on R-series grants; consider alternative justifications or appropriate activity codes (e.g., P-mechanisms) if administrative support must be funded. Institutions sometimes reclassify admin roles under research titles—be cautious and ensure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of special FOAs to direct funds to underfunded institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses special funding opportunities (e.g., AREA/R15, COBRE, IDeA, P20) to direct money to institutions that are not well funded or to entire states that are not well funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These programs are programmatic mechanisms to increase institutional capacity; applicants from under-resourced institutions should identify appropriate FOAs and understand their goals (e.g., capacity-building, center development). P20s are described as preparatory for larger center applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure/transparency around review outcomes and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The outcome of review is not public information. Even study section members have only an imprecise idea of final votes; the final vote is generally within a score range that is overtly stated at the end of discussion and is secret.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect public access to exact review voting records; only summary scores/ranges and administrative outcomes may be available. This limits external auditing of reviewer decisions.
